summary.title: Disagreement over discipline of our son
summary.what_happened: Our son Aram is 9. Last night at 8pm he had not done his maths homework. My husband Daniel raised his voice, called him lazy, and took away his tablet for two weeks. In front of Aram, I told Daniel he was overreacting. Then I took Aram to his room and let him keep the tablet for that night.
summary.my_feelings: I felt upset by how Daniel spoke to Aram. I felt unable to say more in front of our son. I think Daniel may feel I am too soft and that I undermine him.
summary.my_needs: I need Daniel to handle these moments more calmly. I need us to decide rules for Aram together.
summary.desired_outcome: Daniel is calmer with Aram, and we agree on rules together instead of one of us deciding alone.

consult.text:
It sounds like you felt torn last night. You were upset by how Daniel spoke to Aram, and you were also trying to say something without making it worse in front of him. That is a hard spot.

Daniel may see this differently. He may have been worried about the homework and felt the evening was already tense. He may have wanted to act firmly and then felt you were working against him in front of Aram. That could make him feel alone as a parent, and louder because of it.

One thing that may have made this harder is how things happened in the moment. Telling Daniel he was overreacting in front of Aram, and then letting Aram keep the tablet, may have shown Aram that you and Daniel disagree. It may also have left Daniel feeling that his decision did not count. Your concern about the shouting and the word "lazy" is still fair. Both can be true.

We do not know how often homework has been a problem, or how Daniel felt afterwards.

Some next steps:
1. Pick a calm time, away from Aram, to talk with Daniel.
2. Start with your worry about the tone, and say what you would do differently in front of Aram.
3. Ask Daniel what he is worried about, then agree together on homework and screen rules.
So you're saying it's my fault for defending my son?

No. Wanting to protect Aram is a good instinct, and your concern about the shouting is fair. I am not saying the whole problem is your fault.

I am saying that how it happened may have added to the tension. Disagreeing with Daniel in front of Aram, then changing the outcome, may have left Daniel feeling overruled. That does not cancel out how he spoke to Aram. It is one part of a bigger picture, and both of you have a part in it.

You may feel stuck, because it seemed there was no good option in the moment. That is understandable. The useful question now is how the two of you want to handle it next time.

One step could be to agree on a signal or a short pause, so either of you can ask to talk privately. Another is to write down a few simple rules for homework and screens together. You can still tell Daniel plainly that the shouting upset you. Doing it calmly, and away from Aram, is more likely to be heard.

share_draft: Hi Daniel. I want to talk about what happened with Aram's homework last night. I was upset by how loud things got, and by the word "lazy". I also know I told you that you were overreacting in front of Aram, and then let him keep the tablet. I think that made it harder for you. I'd like us to be on the same side with him. I'd like us to agree on rules for homework and screens together, so neither of us has to decide alone. How did the evening look from your side? I'd like to hear it.

perspective_summary: This person is worried about how their husband spoke to their 9-year-old son when homework was not done, and wants him to be calmer. They also accept that disagreeing with him in front of the child may have undermined him. They think he may see them as too soft. They want the two of them to agree on rules together instead of one deciding alone.
